thread:
Sarah (AE): Hey team — FinCore asking for a POC checklist. They want Private/VPC option, but are worried about TLS cert chain and whether our edge proxy will terminate client certs or passthrough. also need firewall rules + confirmation on whether SNAT will break session affinity.
Mike (SE): Quick summary: two viable topologies — PrivateLink (interface endpoint) or VPC peering. PrivateLink = our service endpoint in their VPC (good for isolation). Peering = full L3. TLS behavior differs: with PrivateLink we terminate at our backend or optionally can pass TCP to a customer proxy if they run one.
Sarah (AE): They specifically require: 1) evidence that client certs (mTLS) presented by their app will be validated end-to-end 2) list of ports/fqdn/ips to open in corp firewall 3) any SNAT behavior that would change source ip visible to their app.
Raj (NetOps): TL;DR — If you use PrivateLink (interface endpoint) pointing at our connector in their VPC, traffic enters our connector and then is proxied to Redwood backplane. For mTLS we support two modes: 
- TLS terminate at connector (we validate client cert and then mTLS to our control plane)
- TLS passthrough (TCP tunnel), upstream node validates cert.
Mode chosen determines where cert chain is verified. If they need full end-to-end proof we recommend passthrough + tcp-proxy mode so their backend sees client cert.
Helena (Security): For our compliance questionnaire they want the cert chain path diagram and whether intermediate certs are validated against OS/trusted CA set or against an allowlist. We validate against system CAs by default but can accept explicit CA bundles for the connector.
Mike (SE): Ports & FQDNs:
- Egress to our managed backplane (if using connector): outbound TCP 443 to *.redwood-inference.com (we'll provide exact IP ranges for prod)
- If using PrivateLink only: no public egress required except for initial management (443)
- If peering: allow app -> connector subnet over custom ports (443 or configured port)
Sample firewall allowlist snippet they can paste: 
```
# allow outbound to Redwood backplane (TLS)
ALLOW TCP 443 to redwood-inference.com (resolve FQDN)
# if pinned by IP (example):
ALLOW TCP 443 to 34.198.23.45, 52.14.67.89
```
Sarah (AE): They also asked about SNAT. If we run a connector in their VPC, will requests to their backend appear from our connector IP or preserve original client src-ip?
Raj (NetOps): In connector-forwarding (we terminate and re-issue requests) we will SNAT — source becomes connector ENI IP. With TCP passthrough and route-based forwarding they can preserve client src-ip. Important: some cloud-managed NAT gateways will translate for cross-AZ traffic; recommend a quick validation test.
Mike (SE): Suggest this quick test for them to run in POC (curl with client cert):
```bash
curl --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://10.0.5.12/health -v
```
If connector is in passthrough mode the backend should show the TLS subject and original src. If terminate-mode, backend will see connector IP and our header X-Forwarded-Client-Cert (we can enable).
Helena (Security): We can provide an example attestation doc: cert chain validation + CRL/OCSP checking behavior. They asked about OCSP stapling support — yes, our runtime respects OCSP stapling and will perform OCSP/CRL checks if enabled on the connector.
Sarah (AE): Pricing asks: they want to know whether PrivateLink + connector incurs extra egress or managed connector fees. Quote please — also whether NAT egress bytes billed to them.
Mike (SE): Pricing notes: PrivateLink connector = one-time setup + hourly connector charge (will follow up to attach pricing sheet). Egress to our hosted models billed per-token if using hosted route; if connector forwards to customer's on-prem model, network egress billed per standard cloud transfer (their account). For POC we can offer usage credits for egress.
Sarah (AE): Can we provide a preconfigured Security/Network runbook for their network team? They prefer a single pasteable checklist.
Mike (SE): I'll create a short runbook and attach the internal Connectors playbook. Will include: expected ports, FQDNs, SNAT notes, testing curl steps, and cert bundle instructions.
Raj (NetOps): One more gotcha — if they have TLS‑inspecting corporate proxy (MITM), it will break client cert passthrough. Call this out.
deploy-bot: Ticket REDWOOD-POC-872 created — attach connector IP ranges + temporary test certs for FinCore.
Sarah (AE): thanks. Mike — can you include the sample header config (X-Forwarded-Client-Cert) and example firewall rules in the runbook? Also, we need the exact IP ranges for today so their net team can open them before tomorrow's call.
Mike (SE): Will do. I’ll DM the pricing sheet and post the runbook here by EOD.
Helena (Security): I’ll add the attestation paragraph for OCSP/CRL and the CA bundle instructions.
Raj (NetOps): I'll prepare the mini-test VM manifest (one-liner cloud-init) they can spin up to validate src ip preservation.
Sarah (AE): Perfect — meeting scheduled 1400 UTC tomorrow with FinCore netsec. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
